name: core--rocketchat-portainer-version-pinning
description: RocketChat, its MongoDB and Portainer are pinned to the newest upstream release of each, and the two defects that let Portainer sit on an unmaintained release for seven months are removed. Newest is chosen over the LTS lines only because a retreat to LTS was verified in upstream source for all three, not assumed: RocketChat 8.5.2 and 8.7.0 ship an identical migration set so the downgrade is a pin change; MongoDB 8.3 -> 8.2 is a documented adjacent downgrade while FCV stays at 8.2, which the play now asserts; Portainer 2.39.6 has no database-is-newer guard and starts against a 2.44.0 database, though the clean route is restoring the backup Portainer writes before every migration. Portainer moves from portainer/portainer-ce:latest (which resolved to 2.33.6 from 2026-01-28 on the live host) to a digest pin of 2.44.0. RocketChat moves from the Docker Official Image rocket.chat:8.4.3 to docker.io/rocketchat/rocket.chat:8.7.0 — a repository change, not just a tag bump, because the official image had no 8.4.5, 8.5.2, 8.6.x or 8.7.0 at all. MongoDB moves 8.2.4 -> 8.3.8. Applied to vm700 on 2026-08-17 and verified live: Portainer 2.44.0, RocketChat 8.7, MongoDB 8.3.8 with FCV still 8.2 and the migrations control document still at 335, all reachable through the Caddy edge

implementation.change: portainer.yaml pins portainer_image by OCI index digest (sha256:f49255cd9378827fadfde46062ad0395050237c51d03a93a3dc1dbc6050dda3e = 2.44.0), sets pull and image_name_mismatch explicitly, asserts the pin contains @sha256:, and reads /api/status back to fail the play when the running version does not equal portainer_image_version. rocketchat.yaml gains a pre-upgrade mongodump gated on rc-mongo already running, renders the new templates/rocketchat/docker-compose.yml.j2 instead of copying the static files/rocketchat/docker-compose.yml (deleted), drops the 'Render .env file (if needed)' task that rendered a template which has never existed in this repo under ignore_errors, and adds a 300s health gate, a version assert on /api/info and an assert that MongoDB featureCompatibilityVersion is still 8.2 so the 8.3 -> 8.2 downgrade cannot be closed off silently. defaults/main.yaml gains portainer_* and rocketchat_* blocks carrying both the lifecycle reasoning and the retreat procedure for each pin, including the exact 2.39.6 digest to revert to. tasks/main.yaml tags the RocketChat import rocketchat_stack. Full plan, refutation analysis and per-component retreat in roles/ops-settings/docs/rocketchat-portainer-upgrade.md
implementation.supersedes: No prior eval covers rocketchat.yaml or portainer.yaml. 017 references caddy_portainer_port and caddy_rocketchat_port only as backend addresses; those ports are unchanged, so 017 is not invalidated

EVIDENCE (read-only, 2026-08-17): the defect this fixes is measured, not hypothesised. vm700 /api/status reported Version 2.33.6 from a container created 2026-01-28T22:50:52Z, while Docker Hub's portainer-ce:latest had moved to 2.39.6 on 2026-08-13. community.docker.docker_container defaults to pull: missing, which is why the tag never re-resolved

EVIDENCE (read-only, 2026-08-17): hub.docker.com returns 404 for library/rocket.chat tags 8.4.5, 8.5.2, 8.6.0, 8.6.1, 8.7.0 and 8.0.8, and 200 for 8.4.3, 8.4.4 and 8.5.1. docker.io/rocketchat/rocket.chat has all of them. The repository change is required, not cosmetic

EVIDENCE (upstream source, 2026-08-17): the RocketChat retreat is verified rather than assumed. migrateDatabase() in apps/meteor/server/lib/migrations.ts throws 'Can't find migration version N' outside its try block when the database's control version is absent from the running binary's migration list, which is the crash-loop a real downgrade produces. Tags 8.4.3, 8.4.5, 8.5.2, 8.6.1 and 8.7.0 each carry 42 migration files with highest version v335 and an empty set difference, and the live migrations control document already reads version 335. The upgrade runs zero migrations and 8.5.2 would hit 'Already at target migration version'

EVIDENCE (upstream source, 2026-08-17): the Portainer retreat is verified and is the weakest of the three. 2.39.6 has no database-is-newer guard: NeedsMigration() in api/datastore/migrator/migrate_ce.go returns true on a non-zero unrecognised migrator count, MigrateData() in api/datastore/migrate_data.go calls store.Backup("") before altering anything, and Migrate() finds no migration newer than the 2.44.0 stamp, runs none, and re-stamps SchemaVersion to 2.39.6. migrate_2_43_0, migrate_2_43_sources and migrate_2_44_0 exist only in 2.44.0 and are not reverted, so the clean route is restore-then-run

EVIDENCE (vendor docs + live host, 2026-08-17): the MongoDB retreat is documented and conditional. MongoDB supports single-version downgrades between adjacent releases (8.3 -> 8.2) when the FCV is already at the target; the live rc-mongo reports FCV 8.2, mongod never raises FCV on its own, and neither Rocket.Chat nor this role calls setFeatureCompatibilityVersion

EVIDENCE (read-only, 2026-08-17): the cost of choosing newest is recorded. Rocket.Chat's signed supported-versions JWT marks 8.7.0 lts=false expiring 2027-02-28 against 8.5.x lts=true expiring 2027-06-30. Portainer 2.44.0 STS reached end of maintenance in Aug 2026 and predates the Go 1.25.12, go-git 5.19.2, oras-go 2.6.2, otel 1.44.0 and x/net 0.56.0 CVE remediations that 2.39.6 carries. 2.45 LTS has not shipped — GitHub releases tops out at 2.44.0 and Docker Hub 404s for 2.45.0

EVIDENCE (read-only, 2026-08-17): capacity is not a constraint. /var/lib/docker 93 GB free of 196 GB, / 64 GB free of 79 GB, 10.4 GB RAM available of 16 GB, rocketchat database 60 MB data / 22 MB storage. No image is built by this change

refutation: REFUTED 'bump the compose file to rocket.chat:8.7.0': that tag 404s. The compose referenced the Docker Official Image, whose newest tag was 8.5.1 on 2026-08-17. Every release from the 2026-07-10 security-hotfix wave onward was unreachable from it

REFUTED 'newest release is the most patched' for Portainer: 2.44.0 predates 2.39.6 by thirteen days and is missing six CVE remediations. Survives for Rocket.Chat, where 8.7.0 carries SAML SSO and forged-ephemeral-message fixes that have no 8.5.3 backport yet
REFUTED 'portainer-ce:latest keeps Portainer current': it produced an install that was simultaneously unpinned and frozen — no version in the repo to review, and no pull to move it
REFUTED 'the release notes require MongoDB 8.0, so downgrade': it is a floor, and acting on the misreading would have forced a dump-and-restore, because FCV 8.2 data files cannot be opened by 8.0
REFUTED 'the role can already do this safely': no backup, a permanently failing .env task masked by ignore_errors, and no tag to run the stack in isolation

PARTLY REFUTED 'rollback means re-pinning the old version': true for Portainer, false for Rocket.Chat and MongoDB. The difference is only visible in upstream source and vendor downgrade docs, and it is what makes taking the newest release of each defensible
SURVIVED 'Caddy keeps routing to Portainer': HTTP on 9000 is not in Portainer's deprecated-and-removed table and force-HTTPS-only is opt-in, so caddy_portainer_port needs no change
SURVIVED '8.4.3 -> 8.7.0 may need intermediate hops': the no-skipping rule is about major versions, and the identical migration sets confirm it independently
known_deltas: Portainer 2.44.0 is past its STS end of maintenance and is the less patched of the two candidates. It is pinned because the request was for the newest release of each component; 2.39.6 LTS is strictly safer and the exact digest to revert to is recorded in defaults/main.yaml

MongoDB 8.3.8 is inside Rocket.Chat's supported range ('8.0 and above') but outside what it verifies ('verified with 8.2'), and is a rapid minor release MongoDB publishes for on-premises use only for specific use cases

The RocketChat retreat reverses schema but not content. Settings registered only by 8.7.0 and anything 8.7-only features persisted are additive and do not gate startup, but they are not removed by downgrading; the mongodump is the only artifact that reverses content written while 8.7.0 was live

The RocketChat services still carry no mem_limit, while caddy and omniroute both do because this host has been swapped to death twice. Sizing that ceiling requires observed RSS on 8.7.0 and is deliberately not guessed during a version upgrade
Rocket.Chat /api/info reports major.minor only, so the version assert checks the 8.7 line rather than the 8.7.0 patch. The patch is fixed by the image pin, which the compose render covers

rocketchat_stack is deliberately not changed=0 idempotent — the pre-upgrade dump runs on every play. A backup taken only when someone remembers to ask for one is the backup that is missing when it matters
defects_found_and_fixed_during_deploy: pull: not_present is docker_image_pull vocabulary; community.docker.docker_container takes missing/never/always and failed the play with 'value of pull must be one of: never, missing, always, True, False'. Restructured to pull in its own docker_image_pull task, which is what caddy.yaml and omniroute.yaml already do, so the role fetches every pin by one idiom

The docker_compose_v2 task carried pull: always against two exact pins. It re-fetched both manifests on every run and reported changed without recreating anything — a changed that is not a change is how real drift gets missed. Now pull: missing

The dump runs on every play by design, which grows the backup directory by ~9 MB per run. Bounded with rocketchat_backup_keep (10) and a prune task scoped to the play's own rocketchat-*.archive.gz naming
deploy_notes: The first portainer_stack pull died with containerd 'commit failed: rename .../ingest/... no such file or directory'. A manual docker pull of the same digest succeeded immediately afterwards with no build or CI container running. Transient; retry before investigating
Both RocketChat images were pre-pulled by hand with a retry loop before the play, so a repeat of that containerd failure could not land inside the chat downtime window
Downtime was two health-gate retries, roughly 20 seconds, plus container restart
